scenes.headline: How one shared arrow trains a video model
scenes.sub: DiffusionART, reward tilting without the hidden force
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Velvet! A video model gets one score per clip. Here's how this method turns it into a stable update.

scenes.text: Build one reward direction from each prompt's samples, then regress every state the sampler visited toward it.
scenes.say: The idea: build one reward direction per prompt, then nudge every state the sampler visited toward it.

scenes.title: Why the older method needed a crutch

parts.note: the reward direction, from both branches
parts.say: The older method's two branches agree on the reward direction.

parts.note: sampler vs its own samples: no reward in it
parts.say: But each also feels a gap between the sampler and its own re-noised samples.
That gap cancels only where good and bad samples balance.

steps.say: Generate a few videos per prompt, and keep every state the sampler passed through.
A reward model scores each video. Only the scores are used.
Weight each video by its score's distance from the mean, sum, and rescale. That one arrow is the guidance.
Every cached state gets the same target: old velocity plus the arrow. Then two regression steps.

scenes.title: Why two steps, and a brake

items.say: The first step starts on-policy, so it is pure guidance.
The second sees how far each state drifted and pulls it back. No moving average to tune.
A trust region drops states drifting too far outward.

steps.say: On a thirteen billion parameter video model, it reaches the baselines' final training reward with about twelve times fewer GPU hours.

steps.note: steps are not the same unit
steps.say: Count steps instead and the ratios change: this method takes two updates per batch, one baseline takes one.

scenes.title: GPU hours to visual quality 5.5
scenes.say: In the main run: sixty-three GPU hours, against fourteen hundred.

scenes.text: Aggregate the reward first, then assign it: a shared direction survives where per-sample pushes cancel.
scenes.say: Aggregate the reward first, then assign it. A shared direction survives the sum.
A hidden force, one shared arrow, and a second step instead of a crutch.
